headline: Jamaat leader Akhtaruzzaman placed on 1-day remand over airport disorder
summary: A Dhaka court granted police custody for the former MP following allegations of assaulting a security supervisor and obstructing duties at Shahjalal International Airport.
details: A Dhaka court has placed Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mohammad Akhtaruzzaman Ranjan on a one-day remand to be questioned by police regarding a confrontation at Shahjalal International Airport.
The case was filed by a security officer of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) after Akhtaruzzaman allegedly created disorder and assaulted a security supervisor.
The incident occurred on Thursday morning when passengers arriving from Madinah faced delays in receiving luggage and Zamzam water, leading to agitation among some travelers.
According to the case, Akhtaruzzaman aggressively confronted the airport's Executive Director, verbally abused him, and threatened to have personnel 'tied up and beaten'.
He is further accused of making derogatory remarks about the Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister and physically assaulting a security supervisor who asked people not to film in a restricted area.
The former MP was arrested from his home in Dhaka's Cantonment on Friday. Shortly before his arrest, he posted a video on Facebook calling himself a 'struggle for people's rights'.
Akhtaruzzaman, a retired Army major and former MP for Kishoreganj-2, joined Jamaat-e-Islami shortly before the 13th parliamentary election.
The court has ordered police to submit their investigation report by November 10.
caption:

A Dhaka court has placed Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mohammad Akhtaruzzaman Ranjan on a one-day remand to be questioned by police regarding a confrontation at Shahjalal International Airport.

The case was filed by a security officer of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) after Akhtaruzzaman allegedly created disorder and assaulted a security supervisor.

The incident occurred on Thursday morning when passengers arriving from Madinah faced delays in receiving luggage and Zamzam water, leading to agitation among some travelers.

According to the case, Akhtaruzzaman aggressively confronted the airport's Executive Director, verbally abused him, and threatened to have personnel 'tied up and beaten'.

He is further accused of making derogatory remarks about the Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister and physically assaulting a security supervisor who asked people not to film in a restricted area.

The former MP was arrested from his home in Dhaka's Cantonment on Friday. Shortly before his arrest, he posted a video on Facebook calling himself a 'struggle for people's rights'.

Akhtaruzzaman, a retired Army major and former MP for Kishoreganj-2, joined Jamaat-e-Islami shortly before the 13th parliamentary election.

The court has ordered police to submit their investigation report by November 10.

headline_marked: Flydubai [[co-pilot attacked pilot with axe]] in attempted 'terrorist attack'
headline: Flydubai co-pilot attacked pilot with axe in attempted 'terrorist attack'
summary: The aircraft dropped over 16,000 feet in 30 seconds while flying from the UAE to Israel, before passengers and crew subdued the suspect.
details: A flydubai co-pilot, identified as an Omani national named Hammam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked the captain with a crash axe inside the cockpit during flight FZ1073.
The UAE prosecutor general described the incident as an attempted 'terrorist' attack, stating the co-pilot attempted to take control of the aircraft.
Flight-tracking data from Flightradar24 revealed the plane dropped approximately 16,625 feet in just over 30 seconds while flying over Saudi Arabia.
Disaster was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot. A reserve pilot on board took control and landed the plane at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia.
The aircraft was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew, most of whom were Israeli nationals.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the suspect had undergone radical Islamist indoctrination and appeared suicidal, though a specific motive has not yet been established.
Investigations by UAE and Israeli authorities are ongoing to examine the suspect's background, motives, and digital evidence.
caption:
A flydubai co-pilot used a crash axe to attack the captain in an attempted 'terrorist attack' mid-flight.

A flydubai co-pilot, identified as an Omani national named Hammam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked the captain with a crash axe inside the cockpit during flight FZ1073.

The UAE prosecutor general described the incident as an attempted 'terrorist' attack, stating the co-pilot attempted to take control of the aircraft.

Flight-tracking data from Flightradar24 revealed the plane dropped approximately 16,625 feet in just over 30 seconds while flying over Saudi Arabia.

Disaster was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot. A reserve pilot on board took control and landed the plane at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia.

The aircraft was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew, most of whom were Israeli nationals.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the suspect had undergone radical Islamist indoctrination and appeared suicidal, though a specific motive has not yet been established.

Investigations by UAE and Israeli authorities are ongoing to examine the suspect's background, motives, and digital evidence.
